Resolution_Note: Blizzard subsumes duplicate active snowfall/visibility contributions while accumulated snow may persist as local/runtime state.
Cyclone high-wind contributions supersede generic gale contributions in the same scope.
Tornado high-wind contribution supersedes generic gale effects inside its path.
Shared inundation effects deduplicate while Flash Flood contributes high-velocity flow and debris/scour context.
Monsoon regime can increase duration/recurrence context of separately active Heavy Rain.
Rainfall can add water input to a separately active Flood without creating one.
Saturation can increase instability of a separately active Landslide/Mudslide.
Rain can reduce exposed fire spread/persistence but never guarantees extinguishment or erases smoke/damage.
Cyclone wind/pressure can increase separately active Storm Surge severity.
Drought-dried fuels can increase separately active Wildfire spread/persistence.
Active eruption can increase separately represented Volcanic Ash intensity/production.
Seismic ground motion can increase a separately active slope failure.

Scope_Rule: overlap allowed when timescale or water-source context supports both
Resolution_Note: A short flood can occur during a longer drought; shared water-state claims must remain scope/time-qualified.

Scope_Rule: disjoint or nested local scopes allowed
Resolution_Note: A localized tornado may coexist within a larger cyclone context; effect keys deduplicate where scopes overlap.
ENV-11 does not infer a tsunami from an earthquake even when both are physically plausible.
